svg.text: Each panel shows the two populations (individual people, not sample means). Both groups have the same SD.
Study A: huge samples, tiny difference
divides by SE, which shrinks as n grows
divides by SD, which ignores n
Study B: small samples, big difference
divides by SE, which shrinks as n grows
The curves are clearly shifted apart.
divides by SD, which ignores n
The test answers "is the difference real, or just chance?" Cohen's d answers "how big is it?"
Report both: a tiny effect can be significant with a huge sample, and a large effect can miss significance with a small one.
